original_test_intent: Verify every Type 4 L2 Cache Handle is the defined no-information sentinel or resolves to the correct Type 7 L2 cache structure for that processor, including the platform-approved unified/instruction/data and sharing topology, and persists after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 and Type 7 structures, bind processors by socket, resolve each non-sentinel L2 handle, validate the target's level, type, size and approved sharing relationship, reboot and repeat without altering cache configuration.
manual_activity: A user approves the expected L2 cache relationship, attributes, sentinel/shared policy and reboot plan. The core graph validation is automatable.
required_inputs: Approved L2 cache level, unified/instruction/data role, size and sharing topology
Validated raw/decoded Type 4 and Type 7 parser
Approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not change cache controls, CPU state, BIOS settings or firmware.
Preserve raw and decoded Type 4/Type 7 records so handles, target type and L2 attributes remain auditable.
Resolve every non-sentinel handle to exactly one Type 7 target; do not accept label presence as referential integrity.
Judge shared references using the approved CPU/cache design because L2 sharing granularity is platform specific.
Stop on dangling, wrong-level/type or ambiguous targets, unapproved topology drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Build the Type 4-to-Type 7 L2 relationship map, verify target identity/attributes and compare the approved graph before/after reboot.
Do not modify cache behavior, infer undocumented sharing or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve L2 topology/attributes and sentinel/shared-reference rules.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The field label is correct, but the filtered line cannot prove the referenced Type 7 record exists or is an L2 cache with the approved attributes and sharing.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 and Type 7 data, resolve numeric L2 handles and validate target level/type/size and processor-sharing graph.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The L2 Cache Handle scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: L2 CACHE GRAPH AND ATTRIBUTE VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a handle-indexed graph, explicitly process the no-information sentinel, resolve every other L2 reference to Type 7 and validate L2 level, cache role, size and approved sharing before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, CPU/cache topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 cache-handle and Type 7 cache-information semantics, processor/platform cache topology documentation and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds referential integrity plus L2-specific role, size and sharing validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Increases coverage beyond display persistence while retaining the original handle field.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS cache IDs may expose different granularity; they are optional corroboration, not an automatic substitute for SMBIOS links.

project_override_considerations: A platform may model one L2 record per processor, per core cluster or another documented unit; project approval must define that sharing and the target attributes explicitly.
expected_evidence: Approved L2 topology/attribute baseline, sentinel/shared policy and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4/Type 7 records and handle-resolution graph
Per-target evidence for Type 7 level, role, size and approved sharing
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot graph comparison
Engineer verdict with any documented topology exception

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets the L2 handle; required topology detail is a project input, not a contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The complete metadata graph is safely readable; absent baseline and tooling are execution-readiness inputs.
